You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied (tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).

Goal: History Tab Scope

The History for a Project-tab must be filtered down to the project. If History summary per project is not comptuted, enhane the centarl history job to do breakdown

## Summary

**Root cause found:** the central history job already computes a full per-project breakdown — `historyDashboard.cjs`'s `computeDashboard()` returns `days[].byProject`, `byProjectTotals`, and `toolsByProject` keyed by project, sourced from `historyAggregator.cjs`'s per-`(date, encodedCwd)` rollup buckets. No aggregation work was needed there.

The actual bug: those `byProject` keys are the **encoded** cwd slug (e.g. `-home-bilko-Projects-session-manager`, same scheme as `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/`), but `HistoryDashboard.tsx`'s Project-face scoping matched against the **raw, unencoded** `tab.cwd`. That match never succeeds for any project whose path contains a literal `-` in a segment name — including this very repo (`session-manager`) — so Project-face History was silently rendering as if scoped, but empty.

**Fix:** `HistoryDashboard.tsx` now encodes `activeCwd` via the existing `encodeWorkspace()` helper (already used by the Memory tab for the same cwd→slug mirroring) before building the `keep` filter set, so it matches the real key shape returned by `history:dashboard`.

**Also fixed:** updated `HistoryDashboard.navface.test.tsx`'s fixtures, which previously keyed `byProject` by raw cwd strings (masking the bug), to use encoded keys matching production shape, and added a regression test specifically for a dash-containing cwd.

All 6 History tests pass, typecheck is clean, and `lint:selectors` is green.

Pushed to `main` (`479ccbc`). Only committed the two files I actually changed (`HistoryDashboard.tsx` + its test) — left the pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`session-manager-operations/*`, `src/renderer/state/chat.ts`) untouched since they weren't part of this task.

## Summary

Investigation found "Epic's Execution Queue" wasn't a separate nav tab — it was a same-day commit (`481cef1`) that split the single `scheduler` nav item into two genuinely different screens per sidebar face: Home showed only global config ("Scheduler Configs"), Project showed only the PRD queue ("Epic's Execution Queue"). That split had introduced real duplication: the exact same fire-policy/concurrency/threshold controls existed in two places (`SessionManagerConfig`'s "Scheduler policy" section, and `SchedulePanel`'s live PolicyBar).

**Fixed by:**
- `Scheduler.tsx` — removed the `navFace` fork; one screen titled "Scheduler" on both faces. The Queue tab now stacks Options (session pool, fire policy via `SchedulePanel`'s live PolicyBar, architecture summary, on-disk paths) directly above this project's PRD monitoring in one combined scroll. `scopeCwd` derives from the active tab regardless of face (project-scoped when a tab is active, machine-wide otherwise).
- `SessionManagerConfig.tsx` — deleted the duplicate "Scheduler policy" section (fire policy/threshold/concurrency), since `SchedulePanel`'s PolicyBar now sits right below it and already owns those live controls.
- `navGroups.ts` / `LeftNav.tsx` / `learningContent.ts` — dropped the `labelByFace`/`hintByFace` override so the sidebar reads "Scheduler" everywhere; updated doc comments and learning-panel copy accordingly.
- Updated 3 test files (`Scheduler.navface.test.tsx`, `navGroupsHome.test.ts`, `AlmanacSidebar.test.ts`) to assert the merged behavior.

Verified: typecheck clean, full unit suite (1924 tests) green, `lint:selectors` clean. Committed (`119c20d`) and pushed to `origin/main`.

## Status: partially done — no right-click, and no PRD ever requested one

**What exists today** (`src/renderer/components/SchedulePanel.tsx`):
- Each Queue job row already has a button to jump to the owning Epic/session:
  - The `EpicTag` chip in the collapsed row (`SchedulePanel.tsx:843-849`, `data-testid="job-row-prompt-session-chip"`)
  - A "view epic →" button in the expanded row's Actions block (`SchedulePanel.tsx:919-928`, `data-testid="job-row-prompt-session-link"`)
  - Both call the same `navigateToPromptSession` handler (`:786-789`), which opens the Epic in the Terminal view.
- This was delivered by an already-archived PRD (`session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds-archived/807-...md`) — that's the whole ask it covered.

**What's missing:**
- **No right-click / context menu on job rows at all.** `grep onContextMenu` across `SchedulePanel.tsx` and `sched-primitives.tsx` returns nothing — the row is a plain `<button onClick>`, no `onContextMenu` handler.
- No PRD (active, proposed, or archived) anywhere under `scheduler/**/prds*/` mentions "right click," "context menu," or a job-row session button — this was never queued as a task, so there's nothing "in progress" to check on.

**Precedent to build from, if you want this added:**
- The app has 3 existing right-click implementations to model from: `FileTree.tsx:544,663`, `FileTabBar.tsx:88`, and `EpicQueue.tsx:117` (right-click on the Build toolbar button, from the just-landed PRD 924).
- `EpicQueue.tsx`'s `RowMenu`/`useRowMenuItems` (`:191-497`) is a click-triggered "..." dropdown on Epic rows (separate from Scheduler's Queue) that already has a "Resume in terminal" action — the closest existing template for "row → open session" menu items, just not wired to Queue job rows or triggered by right-click.

Since there's no queued work item for this, I didn't implement anything — this was a status check. If you want it built (right-click on a Queue job row → context menu with "show session" / "open in terminal"), say so and I'll build it directly or queue it as a PRD.
Pushed `ab0b1c8` ("feat(epics): add discuss-first advanced path to Build toolbar button") to `origin/main`. Branch is now up to date with remote — nothing else was ahead.
